runtime_seconds.description: Number of seconds to run the test.

memory_copy_threads.description: Number of memory copy threads to run.

cpu_threads.description: Number of memory CPU stress threads to run.

logfile.description: Log output to file. If empty, no log file is specified.

degraded_mode.description: Run in degraded mode on incompatible systems (-A).

invert_threads.description: Number of memory invert threads to run.

memory_pagesize.description: Size in bytes of memory chunks. 0 for default.

block_devices.description: List of block devices for disk stress testing. Each item is a flat map of options for -d flags.

disk_files.description: List of temporary filenames for disk stress testing (-f flags).

network_targets.description: List of IP addresses for network stress testing (-n flags).

listen.description: Run threads that listen for incoming net connections (--listen).

cc_inc_count.description: Number of times to increment the cacheline's member.

cc_line_count.description: Number of cache line sized datastructures to allocate.

cc_line_size.description: Size of cache line to use as basis for cache coherency test data structures.

find_files.description: Find locations to do disk IO automatically (--findfiles).

force_errors.description: Inject false errors to test error handling (--force_errors).

force_errors_like_crazy.description: Inject a lot of false errors to test error handling (--force_errors_like_crazy).

local_numa.description: Choose memory regions associated with each CPU to be tested by that CPU (--local_numa).

max_errors.description: Exit early after finding specified number of errors.

monitor_mode.description: Only do ECC error polling, no stress load (--monitor_mode).

no_errors.description: Run without checking for ECC or other errors (--no_errors).

paddr_base.description: Allocate memory starting from this address.

remote_numa.description: Choose memory regions not associated with each CPU to be tested by that CPU.

stop_on_errors.description: Stop after finding the first error (--stop_on_errors).
